note: The source of truth for this language's strings. Edit by hand; test/strings.test.mjs checks the two languages against each other (same keys, placeholders in each language's own order, no accidental duplicate text). The tables were first generated from the Swift app's String Catalog on 2026-09-21, before that app was retired to the mac branch.

strings.chart.hint.days: Point at a day to read its totals; click one to filter the cards above.
strings.chart.hint.lines: Point at a week to read each project's shares with the number of lines behind them.
strings.chart.hint.weeks: Point at a week to read its totals; click one to filter the cards above.
strings.contract.note: Nothing is drawn from a schema this build does not understand.
strings.contract.title: Prudence cannot read this store
strings.engine.busy: A run is already going. Wait for it to finish.
strings.engine.error.failed: It ran and stopped with an error.
strings.engine.error.noVersion: That file does not answer `--version` as the Prudence engine.
strings.engine.error.notExecutable: That file is not something this app can run.
strings.engine.failed.detail: The engine stopped in a way this version does not recognise.
strings.engine.failed.title: The engine did not finish
strings.engine.ingestFinished.sessions: Ingest finished. The store now holds %1$@.
strings.engine.install.done: Installed. Looking for the engine again.
strings.engine.install.manual: Run these two in a terminal, in this order. The first installs uv; the second installs the engine with it.
strings.engine.install.noUv: uv is not in any directory this app looks in, so there is nothing to run.
strings.engine.noShell.detail: This page is open without the app around it, so nothing has looked for the engine. Run the app to see where it is.
strings.engine.notFound.detail: Nothing can be ingested or reviewed until it is found. Choose the file yourself if it is installed somewhere this search does not look.
strings.engine.versionMismatch: The engine on this machine is version %1$@, and the store was last written by %2$@. Both still read; the next ingest will be written by %1$@.
strings.menu.reviewNotReady: Not enough new work for a review yet.
strings.observation.sentence.alive: %1$@, your %2$@ sessions %3$@ still have %4$@ of their lines at head (median); the %5$@ %6$@, %7$@.
strings.observation.sentence.rework: %1$@, your %2$@ sessions %3$@ reworked %4$@ of their lines (median); the %5$@ %6$@, %7$@.
strings.observation.split.commit_attempts_per_co: that attempted more than two commits for each commit counted
strings.observation.split.context_resets: that replayed an earlier session's records
strings.observation.split.files_edited_unread: that edited more files before reading them than your median here
strings.observation.split.hand_edits_between_tur: that changed the tree by hand between two turns the hooks saw
strings.observation.split.prompts_per_active_hou: that prompted more often per active hour than your median here
strings.observation.split.repeated_errors: that hit the same error three times or more
strings.observation.split.sittings: that ran over three or more sittings
strings.observation.split.tests_before_commit: that ran tests before at least half of their commits
strings.observations.allSessions: Every row here is computed over every session on record, not over a date range.
strings.observations.empty.all.detail: An observation needs enough sessions on both sides of a threshold, and a wide enough gap between the two medians. No behaviour in this store clears both floors yet. Nothing is wrong with your store.
strings.observations.empty.all.title: No observations yet
strings.observations.empty.pooled.detail: Nothing yet holds across your projects. Choose a project above to see the rows computed from its own sessions.
strings.observations.empty.pooled.title: No pooled observations
strings.observations.empty.project.detail: No behaviour here clears both floors: at least five sessions on each side of the split, and enough distance between the two medians to be worth printing.
strings.observations.empty.project.title: No observations for this project
strings.observations.floor: An observation splits your own sessions in two at one threshold and takes each side's median. These are descriptions of what happened, not advice.
strings.observations.method: Both figures on a card are medians the engine took, one per side of the split, read from the app_observation view: with_value over with_n sessions and without_value over without_n sessions, with coverage, fact_commits and inferred_commits from the same row. The app prints them and derives nothing from them.
strings.observations.method.threshold: The engine's own words for this split: %1$@.
strings.observations.scope.pooled: The rows that hold across your projects come first; each project's own follow under its name. A pooled row is computed for a behaviour no single project had the sessions to answer, and is not a finding about any one of them.
strings.observations.scope.project: Rows computed from this project's own sessions alone.
strings.observations.sortedByGap: The behaviour whose two medians are furthest apart comes first. That is how the list is arranged, not a ranking of what matters.
strings.observations.subtitle.pooled: Across your projects first, then one group per project. Choose a project for its own.
strings.overview.noHours.detail: No session in this range recorded any active minutes. A Claude Code version that writes no usage fields leaves this empty, which is not the same as no work.
strings.overview.noHours.title: No active time in this range
strings.overview.noOutcomes.detail: No commit in this range is credited with a line that could be followed. A repository where other people commit has its outcomes withheld rather than guessed.
strings.overview.noOutcomes.title: No outcomes to follow yet
strings.overview.noTokens.detail: Nothing here measured any tokens. A Claude Code version that wrote no usage fields is not zero tokens; it is no measurement at all.
strings.overview.noTokens.title: No tokens in this range
strings.overview.tokensByPurpose.method: Summed from the app_usage_by_purpose_day view into the ISO week each local day falls in, over total_tokens.
strings.overview.tokensByPurpose.note2: What each week's tokens went on. A session counts on the day it started; a week nothing was recorded in is left empty rather than drawn as zero.
strings.overview.tooFewWeeks.detail: A trend needs two measured weeks. %1$@ so far; the table below has it in full.
strings.overview.tooFewWeeks.title: Not enough weeks to draw a line yet
strings.overview.whatBecame: What became of each week's work
strings.overview.whatBecame.method: alive_30d / measured_30d and reworked / lines, both from the app_outcomes_by_week view; the band is that view's coverage.
strings.overview.whatBecame.note2: Of the lines written in a week, how many were still in the code thirty days later, and how many had been rewritten. The pale band behind them is how much of that week's committed work the sessions themselves wrote. A week whose thirty days are not up yet is a gap, never a zero.
strings.overview.whatBecame.note2Weekly: Of the lines written in a week, how many were still in the code thirty days later, and how many had been rewritten. The pale band behind them is how much of that week's committed work the sessions themselves wrote. A week whose thirty days are not up yet is a gap, never a zero. This card stays weekly under every range, because the engine measures an outcome per week and there is no daily figure to draw.
strings.overview.whereTime.method: Active minutes per local day, summed from the app_usage_by_purpose_day view.
strings.overview.whereTime.note2: Which days the work happened on. A darker square is a longer day; a day with no session at all is left blank rather than shaded as zero.
strings.review.became.note: Of the lines written by the commits in the outcome window, how many were still there later and how many you rewrote. Every share carries the number of lines it is over, and the pale underlay behind each bar is how much of that work the sessions themselves wrote.
strings.review.compared.note: The same figures over the period of the same length immediately before this one. A period that measured nothing is a dash, never a zero.
strings.review.coverageHelp: The mean share of a counted commit's added lines the session itself wrote, over the commits in the outcome window.
strings.review.coverageUnderlay: The pale underlay behind each bar is that figure's coverage.
strings.review.did.coverageFoot: over the commits credited to these sessions
strings.review.did.coverageHelp: The mean share of a counted commit's added lines the session itself wrote, over the commits credited to the sessions of the period reviewed.
strings.review.did.note: The sessions of the period, grouped by the purpose their tool mix was labelled with, and the commits credited to them. A dash is a session that recorded no usage fields at all, which is not zero tokens.
strings.review.empty.detail: A review is written on demand and kept. Press Review now, or run `prudence review` in a terminal; it needs a few new sessions and one commit that has crossed seven days.
strings.review.empty.title: No review yet
strings.review.emptyForProject.detail: Your other projects' reviews are still there: choose All projects above. `prudence review --project %1$@` writes one for this project.
strings.review.emptyForProject.title: No review of %1$@ yet
strings.review.figuresHelp: Every number on this page, each one re-derivable from the CLI.
strings.review.headline: Review %1$@, %2$@ to %3$@
strings.review.notReady.title: Not ready for a review yet
strings.review.notWired: Review now runs the engine, and that wiring arrives with the next delivery. Until then, `prudence review` in a terminal writes one.
strings.review.observations.note: Each row splits your own sessions in two at one threshold and takes each side's median. They describe what happened; they are not advice, and neither side is the better one.
strings.review.observations.stored: The sentences as the review stored them
strings.review.provenance: Every figure above is computed from your own record: %1$@ numbers, each re-derivable with `prudence usage`, `prudence outcomes` or `prudence observations` over the same range.
strings.review.rangeLine: Period reviewed: %1$@ to %2$@. Outcomes are measured over a different window: the commits made between %3$@ and %4$@.
strings.review.segment.checked: Every number in it was checked against the review's own figures.
strings.review.segment.none: No model segment was written for this review. `prudence review --explain` writes one, and every figure in it has to be one of the review's own numbers.
strings.review.subtitle.none: No review has been written yet.
strings.review.suggestions.note: What became of the suggestions an earlier review left open.
strings.review.unknownSection: A section this version of the app does not lay out; here it is as stored.
strings.review.unreadable.detail: The stored JSON is not in a shape this build understands. The row above is still true; only its body is unreadable.
strings.review.unreadable.title: This review's sections cannot be read
strings.scope.project.help: Every figure below is for this project alone.
strings.scope.range.help: How far back the charts look. Up to sixty days they are drawn per day, and beyond that per week.
strings.settings.about.method: The app's version is this build's own. The engine's is app_status.engine_version, which is the version that last wrote to the store.
strings.settings.about.note: Which pieces are running, and where the project is.
strings.settings.about.platform.note: What the shell reports about this machine, in its own words. Worth quoting when something about the window looks wrong.
strings.settings.appearance.note: Light and dark. System follows this machine's own setting and changes with it; the other two hold whatever you choose.
strings.settings.databasePath.resolved: Found the way the engine finds it: PRUDENCE_DATA_DIR when that is set, and this system's standard location otherwise.
strings.settings.enginePath.note: Looked for in uv's bin directories, then Homebrew, then your login shell. Install it below if it is not on this machine yet.
strings.settings.general.note: How this app behaves on this machine. Everything here is the app's own; the engine's settings are on the Model tab and in config.toml.
strings.settings.language.note: The strings of this interface, in both windows, without a relaunch. The engine's own sentences and the CLI stay English; this app rebuilds an observation's sentence from the numbers rather than translating it.
strings.settings.model.language.note: The language the engine writes that prose in. This is the engine's own setting, changed here with `prudence config model --language`, and it is not the language of this interface.
strings.settings.model.method: Every line here is one `prudence config model` printed, read as it came. The key is a variable name and never a value; the engine does not print a key and this app does not ask for one.
strings.settings.model.note: Which model the engine would send to, if you asked it to write the optional prose in a review. Pressing a button in this app never calls a model.
strings.settings.model.unread: The engine could not be asked what model it would use.
strings.settings.noShell: This page is open without the app around it, so there is nothing here to change.
strings.settings.openAtLogin.note: Prudence starts with this machine and waits in the menu bar. It opens no window until you ask for one.
strings.settings.openAtLogin.refused: This machine would not register the login item:
strings.settings.store.contract.value: %1$@ in this store; this build reads %2$@.
strings.settings.store.method: last_ingest_at, sessions and the versions below are columns of the app_status view, printed as they are. The path is the file the shell opened.
strings.settings.store.note: Where the record is on this machine. The app opens it read-only and never writes to it; the engine is what writes.
strings.settings.timedIngest.note: The shell runs `prudence ingest` on its own, at this interval, whether or not a window is open. It never starts one while another run is going.
strings.settings.title: Settings
strings.settings.versions.note: Every step of the engine carries a version. A figure re-derived after one of them changed can differ from one computed before it.
